description:
With the midterms one day away, conservative radio host John Fredericks says Donald Trump can still close the deal for Republicans, even as voters struggle with rising costs. In a special episode of America, Actually Vox’s Astead Herndon speaks to the longtime Trump supporter as he defends the president’s record on the economy and Iran, explains why he believes MAGA voters will show up when Trump isn’t on the ballot, and discusses how the movement’s hold on the Republican Party will outlast Trump himself.

author: Vox
description:
Someone else can make you squirm with one touch, but try tickling yourself, and nothing happens. Why? Investigator Konstantina Kilteni went looking for answers and found something surprising. Socrates, Aristotle, Galileo, and Darwin all wondered about tickling, but there’s very little actual research on it. Two millennia later, we still don’t know what ticklishness is for. 

This week on Unexplainable, Noam Hassenfeld asks Konstantina what’s going on in our brains when we get tickled. Watch the full episode on Netflix or listen wherever you get your podcasts.

author: Vox
description:
Silicon Valley says it can build better weapons, faster and cheaper than traditional defense contractors. But what happens when the companies making those weapons also get a say in how they’re used?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today’s episode, Vox reporter and producer Miles Bryan talks with long-time national security journalist Sharon Weinberger, author of Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War. The book traces Silicon Valley’s deep ties to the military and its return to the weapons business through companies like Palantir, SpaceX, and Anduril. Sharon says this raises troubling questions of how private funding gives tech founders greater control over military technology, and whether their promises of innovation justify risks to accountability.
